questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: High academic standards, language I was somewhat comfortable with and the opportunity to experience something new

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have nothing but good things to say about the University and Washington State at large, but it was an insane time to live in the US, both politically, and financially. Quite a few students were partying like there was no tomorrow and the school had a massive gym, a bowling hall and the buildings looked like castles, meanwhile homeless fentynal users slept right on the campus perimeter and populated quite a bit of Seattle downtown. Not a symptom of the University's condition though, nor of Seattle, but more the state of the US at large.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite simple, except the information about my buddy which I didn't seem to get/missed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation with the host uni, a group chat where we could ask questions and connect and also a ton of events that they hosted for the exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Quite a few options, but they're all booked through the uni's system. I can definitely recommend it, though it is probably cheaper going with off campus options

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You had to get a meal plan which I found infuriating, especially since the meal options where comically stereotypically American. You could get healthier options such as salmon and the like at the different restaurants, but the junk food was much better made, and the healthy options were not financially viable to eat every day. There was a kitchen downstairs which I ended up using, dropping the meal plan entirely. Though I then had to pretty much cook with an audience as it was in the dorms reception hall

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They should know about my experience with the meal plans, otherwise it was an okay experience. Very hit or miss who you end up on room with though, and you can almost certainly also find a single room for the same price as the dorms (if you cook yourself)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Simple through their website. I found the sign up information readily available and I was never in doubt as to my options

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I honestly don't know, I figured it out myself

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly successful, although I needed both the prof's and the faculty leader's permission to take a class outside of my faculty, and they flat out sometimes never responded. That caused me to default to my second option for these classes, but once again, that process was fairly comprehensive. The prof's could definitely read mail more often though, and at least have the courtesy to respond

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the information beforehand, that helped me a ton

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were BA level, but I took one class at MA level as it looked fun

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: To me it varies much more by professor to professor than between universities. That is true both in UCPH and UW

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Archeology 101: feeding the world
Dynamical systems and chaos 
Distance and time
Mathematical methods in Classical Mechanics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any class with Prof Chris Laws is fantastic, he's a great guy. Dynamical Systems and Chaos and Mathematical Methods in Classical Mechanics are both demanding courses that were taught well at UW. Public Outreach in Astronomy was extremely useful for learning to present and communicate science, great prof as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A really great massive gym complex, a lovely bundle of clubs and a blossoming social life.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking is fantastic in the region, otherwise you can pick and choose based on interest

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Canada (I went to British Colombia myself) it is really pretty up there. There is also plenty of things to explore in downtown Seattle and Washington State at large, once again based on interest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, though I struggled a bit with the current political climate in the US (the university was more aligned with my views, so it is more the country at large that made me feel unsafe)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them whenever you get the chance! The only fun you have is the one you make for yourself, and the same goes with social opportunities, you should just dive in head first!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Gun laws

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Øhm it was a really accepting culture at the university, accepting you regardless of race, culture, sexuality and non-violent worldviews

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to put on a few kilos unless you cook yourself, grab the chances that arise early on to socialize with the other exchange students as well as the local student, and lastly have fun, even though your surroundings are not always optimal!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not at the moment no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The constant feel of unease, caused by a mixed bag of the lax weapon laws in the US, the obvious difference in wealth plain to see on the streets and the political climate that amongst other things targeted scientific research (local student within my field of physics were leaving off scientific terms such as "cis" and "trans" because funding was getting cut based on buzzwords like these

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
